title: Cookie consent MVP: blocker, banner, regions, cookie policy
body:
## What

Build the cookie consent MVP that replaces Complianz and Complianz Terms & Conditions: hold back scripts and embeds that set cookies until visitors allow them, a theme-matched banner only where needed, and a cookie policy that keeps itself current.

## Why

Complianz needs a scan, a wizard and ongoing upkeep. This plugin should work when switched on: recognise known services in the page as it is sent, decide per visitor in the browser (page-cache safe), and ask only as strictly as each region needs. Legal defaults stay configurable and are not legal advice.

## Scope

- Service registry (categories, URL and inline patterns, cookies, privacy links) and an output-buffer blocker for scripts and iframes, with placeholders and a Load button for embeds.
- Consent feature: settings, region model from the browser time zone (opt-in for Europe, Quebec, unclear; opt-out elsewhere; GPC turns marketing off), Google Consent Mode v2 defaults and updates, WP Consent API, banner and Cookie settings dialog, footer menu link and button, `#cookie-settings` links, Complianz one-off import.
- Cookie policy feature: block and shortcode listing the site's detected cookies, plus privacy policy guide text.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md`, README, readme.txt, changelogs, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md` front-end section; uninstall cleanup.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-services.php`, `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php` (new)
- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-policy.php` (new)
- `includes/views/consent-banner.php`, `assets/js/spcc-head.js`, `assets/js/spcc.js`, `assets/css/spcc.css`, `assets/js/blocks.js` (new)
- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-setup.php`, `uninstall.php`

Reference pattern: features as classes listed in `SEOProCookieConsent_Setup::FEATURES` (`STANDARDS.md`).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4` pass with no PHP messages.
- Browser checks on a test site: Europe time zone holds everything back until Accept/Save/Load; Reject after Accept reloads and stops scripts; US time zone loads with a notice; GPC turns marketing off; dialog keyboard and Escape behaviour; no JS errors.

title: Terms and conditions block (replaces Complianz Terms & Conditions)
body:
## What

A Terms and conditions feature that replaces Complianz Terms & Conditions: a block (and shortcode) that renders plain-English terms from a few answers (business name, country, what the site sells, returns, contact), editable by the site owner.

## Why

The plugin should replace both Complianz plugins (#2). Site owners need terms without a paid generator. Wording is a starting point, not legal advice; say so in the settings and the README.

## Files

- New `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-terms.php`, listed in `SEOProCookieConsent_Setup::FEATURES`.
- Reference pattern: `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-policy.php` (block + shortcode + settings card) and the block helper in `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-setup.php`.
- Import once from Complianz Terms & Conditions options if present (see the Complianz import in `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`).
- README, readme.txt, changelogs; `docs/architecture.md` → Not yet.

## Verification

- On a test site: the block renders with the answers, updates when they change, and the feature is off by default.

title: Local video thumbnails in held-back YouTube and Vimeo placeholders

Loading them from YouTube in the browser would leak the visit before consent, so they must come from the site. ## Files - `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php`: add the thumbnail URL to `.spcc-embed` as a background or ``. - Fetch once per video ID with `wp_remote_get`, save to uploads, keep the attachment or file path in a non-autoloaded option or transient; never fetch during a front-end request (queue for WP-Cron). - `assets/css/spcc.css`: keep text readable over the image (scrim), dark mode. - readme.txt External services: name YouTube/Vimeo thumbnail requests made by the server. ### Files Scope - `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php` - `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-thumbnails.php` - `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php` - `uninstall.php` - `assets/css/spcc.css` - `README.md` - `readme.txt` - `changelog.txt` - `DESIGN.md` - `docs/architecture.md` Integration: register the cron callback with the consent feature; remove owned files, cache options and pending cron events on uninstall. Keep PHP 7.4 / WordPress 6.2 compatibility and existing consent behavior. The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (10 files touched). ### Files in the conflicting PR ``` DESIGN.md README.md assets/css/spcc.css changelog.txt docs/architecture.md includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-thumbnails.php includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php readme.txt uninstall.php ``` ### Worker guidance The prior PR's head commit is `6dc674746d6f7967aeee732d595b08e301aac268`. Choose the cheapest path that works: 1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale): ```bash git fetch origin pull/22/head:recovered-22 # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802). git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main cd ../fresh-worktree git cherry-pick 6dc674746d6f7967aeee732d595b08e301aac268 # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR ``` 2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic. 3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch. 4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #22's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong. Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`. _Routed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)._

title: Optional consent records with export and expiry
body:
## What

Optional consent records: store each choice (anonymous ID from the consent cookie, categories, services, model, time, policy version) so a site owner can show proof of consent, with an export and automatic deletion after the consent lifetime.

## Why

GDPR Article 7(1) asks controllers to be able to show consent was given. Complianz offers records in Pro. Off by default, because it adds a write per choice and personal data.

## Files

- `assets/js/spcc.js` `save()`: send the choice to a REST route (only when the feature is on; use `navigator.sendBeacon`).
- New REST route and storage (custom table or a CPT with autoload-free meta; follow `STANDARDS.md` → Performance and migrations), cleanup in WP-Cron, removal in `uninstall.php`.
- Settings under the Consent card; export as CSV.
- `docs/architecture.md` → Consent cookie (add the record ID) and → Not yet.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (query counts stay within limits).
- Test site: choices are recorded only when the feature is on; export lists them; records older than the lifetime are deleted by cron; uninstall removes them.

### Files Scope

- `assets/js/spcc.js`
- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php`
- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-setup.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`
- `uninstall.php`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

Implementation follows the existing Consent settings schema and plugin-owned setup loader. Use an indexed per-site table, bounded cron cleanup and streamed keyset-paged CSV export. Validate on WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4 and current WordPress; no core files or legal/region defaults change. PR #24 touches consent boot/uninstall/docs for thumbnails; preserve that independent work when integrating.

title: Hold back scripts and iframes added after page load (lightboxes)
body:
## What

Hold back scripts and iframes added after page load (lightboxes, sliders, tabbed embeds, page builders that inject iframes from templates or JSON), not only those in the HTML as sent.

## Why

The output-buffer blocker (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php`) only sees the initial HTML. A YouTube lightbox inserts its iframe on click and loads without consent.

## Files

- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: a `MutationObserver` (started before other scripts run) that checks added `script` and `iframe` elements against the service patterns sent in the config, and holds back matches the same way the server does (`type="text/plain"`, `data-spcc-src`, placeholder for iframes).
- Patterns for the browser: add them to the front config in `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php` (keep it small: hosts only).
- `docs/architecture.md` → Holding back.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Test site, Europe time zone: a page that inserts a YouTube iframe and a GA script with JS after load shows a placeholder and does not request either until allowed; no JS errors; no measurable delay on pages without matches.

### Files Scope

- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`
- `assets/js/spcc.js`
- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

Implementation integration: `spcc.js` owns banner discovery and release, so it must consume dynamic matches and restore held script sources. Use compact URL match fragments rather than broadening shared hosts (Google hosts also serve necessary security scripts); do not ship built-in inline-code signatures. The observer needs synchronous insertion/source guards because notification occurs after script execution or network dispatch. Preserve exclusions, Google advanced mode, and page-builder editor bypasses. User documentation and changelogs are required by STANDARDS.md. PR #20 touches the consent feature and documentation for settings, but does not implement dynamic blocking; keep edits localized to config/head activation.

title: Move here: settings, blocked scripts, policy pages and visitor consent from other cookie plugins
body:
A site switching to SEO Pro Cookie Consent keeps what it set up in its old cookie plugin (settings, the scripts it blocked, its policy pages) and its visitors' existing choices. Then, with guidance, it removes the old plugin and everything it left behind. Same approach as SEO Pro Stats' "Move here" work (wpallstars/seoprostats#108), adapted to cookie plugins.

## Goal

1. **Detection by data, not just by plugin**: a source is listed whenever its data is on the site (options, tables, pages using its shortcodes or blocks), whether the plugin is active, inactive or already deleted.
2. **Import tab** (Settings → SEO Pro Cookie Consent → Import): for each source, a dry run (settings that would change, scripts and services it blocked, pages that use its documents, consent cookie it set), then import, and undo per import.
3. **Settings**: equivalent settings (regions, banner position and message, consent lifetime, policy page, Consent Mode) are filled only where ours still have their defaults, shown in the dry run first.
4. **Scripts**: the source's own blocked-script and whitelist entries go into Also hold back and Never hold back; services it lists that we already recognise are noted, not duplicated.
5. **Visitors are not asked again**: a visitor who already chose in the old banner keeps that choice. The browser reads the source's consent cookie once, maps its categories to ours, and writes `spcc_consent`, only when the source recorded an explicit choice.
6. **Policy pages keep working**: a page that shows the old plugin's cookie list gets the Cookie policy block instead; other generated documents (privacy statement, terms, imprint) are frozen as editable blocks, so nothing goes blank when the old plugin is deleted.
7. **Guided removal**: after an import, the owner checks the banner and pages, deactivates and deletes the plugin (with its own delete-data setting turned on first if it has one), or uses **Remove leftover data** once it is inactive or gone.
8. **Plugins screen and notices**: while a source has data that is not imported, or leftovers remain, a notice and a note on its row say what to do next.

## Decisions (carried over from SEO Pro Stats; change only with the owner's say)

- **One banner at a time.** Unlike statistics, cookie banners cannot run side by side. Every source plugin goes in the consent feature's `REPLACES` (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`), so our banner and blocking wait while it is active, as Complianz does today. The import runs while the source is still active; deactivating it is what switches visitors over.
- **Remove leftovers on request.** SEO Pro Cookie Consent may delete another plugin's leftover tables and options, but only through the explicit, confirmed Remove leftover data action, and only once that plugin is inactive or deleted. This is a plugin-own exception to `STANDARDS.md` → Structure, recorded in `AGENTS.md`. Imports themselves only read, except pages the owner chooses to convert.
- **Consent carry-over is conservative**: only explicit choices map across; anything unclear asks again.

## Children

Every child after the first is blocked by the first.

1. #11: engine, Import tab, consent carry-over, policy page hand-over, Remove leftover data, WP-CLI, and Complianz (free, Premium, Terms & Conditions). `tier:thinking`
2. #12: Plugins screen and admin notices through the whole cycle. `tier:standard`
3. #13: CookieYes and Cookie Notice & Compliance. `tier:standard`
4. #14: CookieAdmin, GDPR Cookie Compliance and WPConsent. `tier:standard`
5. #15: Real Cookie Banner. `tier:thinking`
6. #16: hosted banners: Cookiebot, iubenda and Termly. `tier:standard`

#11 is blocked by #3 (the consent engine).

Install counts from the WordPress.org API (October 2026): CookieYes 1M+, Complianz 1M+, Cookie Notice 800k+, CookieAdmin 400k+, GDPR Cookie Compliance 300k+, WPConsent 200k+, iubenda 200k+, Real Cookie Banner 100k+, Cookiebot 100k+, Termly 80k+. Smaller plugins (SureCookie, Cookiez, Beautiful Cookie Consent Banner and others) can follow through the `seoprocookieconsent_migrate_sources` filter or later children. Borlabs Cookie is sold outside WordPress.org; add it only with a licence for testing.

## Rules every child follows

- **Visitor pages pay nothing**: detection, import and cleanup run only in wp-admin, WP-CLI or REST. Cache detection in a non-autoloaded option, refreshed when the Import tab or Plugins screen opens. The only front-end part is the consent carry-over in `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: a cookie read, no request.
- **Imports only read** another plugin's data. The only writes are Remove leftover data (confirmed, deletes exactly what it lists, refused while that plugin is active) and page conversion the owner confirms (a revision is kept).
- **Never copy consent records** (IP addresses, user IDs) from a source's log tables; they belong to the old plugin's records and stay until the owner removes them.
- **Verify each source on a real install** of its current version (`scripts/test-site.sh up`, `scripts/test-site.sh wp plugin install <slug> --activate`, set it up, accept and reject in a browser). List its options with `wp option list --search='<prefix>*'`, its tables with `SHOW TABLES`, its cookies from the browser, and name the versions checked in the adapter's docblock. **Verify plugin slugs** with the WordPress.org plugin API.
- **Write as if public**: describe the plugins we import from in our own words, and never copy their code.
- Each source added to `REPLACES` changes the README's replaced-plugins line: run `php scripts/replaced-plugins.php --write`.

## Verification (each child)

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
- On a test site with the source set up (banner position, a custom blocked script, a cookie policy page) and a visitor who accepted statistics only: the dry run lists them; import fills our settings and Also hold back; the policy page shows our block; after deactivating the source, the same visitor sees no banner and statistics only is allowed; a second import changes nothing; undo restores our settings; Remove leftover data deletes exactly the listed items and the notice goes away.

title: Move here 1: import engine, Import tab, consent carry-over, policy pages, leftovers, and Complianz
body:
Parent: #10. Read it first for the goal, the decisions and the rules. This is the first child: the engine, the Import tab, consent carry-over, policy page hand-over, Remove leftover data, and the first source, Complianz (free, Premium, Terms & Conditions). Every other child adds an adapter on top of it.

blocked-by: #3 (the consent engine must be merged first)

## Goal

1. The owner opens Settings → SEO Pro Cookie Consent → **Import** and sees Complianz listed whenever its data is on the site, with what can come across.
2. A dry run lists settings, blocked scripts, pages and the consent cookie mapping; import applies them; the Consent card reflects them.
3. The tab then asks the owner to check the banner and pages, deactivate and delete Complianz, and finally offers **Remove leftover data**.

## Design

### Source adapters

An abstract `SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate_Source`:

- `KEY`, `NAME`, `SLUGS` (plugin folders, free and Pro).
- `detect()`: whether its data is present (options, tables, pages with its shortcodes or blocks), plugin state (active, inactive, not installed). Cheap: known option names and one `SHOW TABLES LIKE`, no content scans beyond a `post_content LIKE` on its shortcode names, limited and cached.
- `settings()`: its options mapped to our setting keys, each with a converter (regions, banner position, message, consent days, policy page, Consent Mode).
- `scripts()`: the scripts it was told to block or allow, as host or path fragments for Also hold back (`category:` prefix when not marketing) and Never hold back.
- `pages()`: pages using its documents: for each, which shortcodes or blocks, and whether each is a cookie list (replace with our Cookie policy block) or another generated document (freeze as static blocks).
- `consent_cookie()`: for the browser: cookie names, how to read an explicit choice, and the category map to ours (`preferences`, `statistics`, `embeds`, `marketing`). Return nothing when the source's cookie cannot be read reliably.
- `leftovers()`: exactly what it leaves: tables (with `$wpdb->prefix`), options (known names or a prefix only it uses, checked on a real install), cron hooks, transients, user meta, upload folders, and pages it created that no longer have content. Only what is present.
- `uninstall_setting()`: its own delete-data-on-uninstall option, if any.

Registry `SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate::sources()`, extended by one class per adapter, plus a `seoprocookieconsent_migrate_sources` filter.

### Import and undo

- Settings go through `import_setting()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-feature.php`), so only defaults are filled. Move the current one-off Complianz import (`SEOProCookieConsent_Consent::migrate()`) into the Complianz adapter, so there is one path.
- Each run stores a record (non-autoloaded option `seoprocookieconsent_imports`): source, time, our settings before, the lines added to Also/Never hold back, pages converted with their revision IDs. **Undo** restores our settings and lines from it and restores page revisions.
- A second run with nothing new changes nothing.

### Consent carry-over

- The front config gets `migrate` entries from adapters whose source data is still present or was imported (only `consent_cookie()` data, a few bytes; none once the owner removes leftovers or turns it off).
- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: when there is no `spcc_consent`, read the source cookie, map an explicit choice to our categories, write `spcc_consent` with `m` from the current model and a `src` key naming the source, then continue as usual. Never treat "banner dismissed" or implied consent as opt-in consent in an opt-in place.
- Only while our feature is running (the source is inactive), so the two never race.

### Policy page hand-over

- The dry run lists each page and what would change. On import (per page, confirmed), replace the cookie list shortcode or block with the Cookie policy block, and replace other generated documents with their rendered HTML in Custom HTML or paragraph blocks, rendered while the source is still active. Keep a revision.
- If the source is already inactive, its shortcodes cannot render: offer only the cookie list replacement and say which documents need rewriting.

### Remove leftover data

`SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate::cleanup($source, $dry_run)`: lists `leftovers()`, deletes exactly that list after confirmation (tab) or `--yes` (WP-CLI). Refused while the plugin is active on this site or network-wide; needs `delete_plugins` and `manage_options`. `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS %i` per listed table, `delete_option()`, `wp_clear_scheduled_hook()`. Multisite: this site only; list network-wide leftovers without deleting. Cannot be undone: the confirmation says so and suggests a backup. Add the one-line exception to `AGENTS.md`.

### Complianz adapter

Verify on a real install of the current Complianz (free) and, if available, Premium and Complianz Terms & Conditions; name versions in the docblock. Expected, to confirm: settings in `cmplz_options` and related `cmplz_*` options; custom blocked scripts and whitelist in its script centre; documents via `[cmplz-document]` shortcodes and its blocks (cookie statement, privacy statement, imprint), and `[cmplz-terms-conditions]` from Terms & Conditions; consent cookies `cmplz_*` per category plus a banner status cookie; tables `cmplz_*`. Add `complianz-terms-conditions` to `REPLACES` only if our Terms feature (#4) exists; otherwise just freeze its page.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate.php`
- NEW: `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-source.php`
- NEW: `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-complianz.php`
- NEW: `includes/admin/class-seoprocookieconsent-import-tab.php`
- NEW: `admin/js/seoprocookieconsent-import.js`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-setup.php`
- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`
- EDIT: `assets/js/spcc-head.js`
- EDIT: `uninstall.php`
- EDIT: `AGENTS.md`
- EDIT: `docs/architecture.md`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`

## Reference pattern

title: Move here 2: Plugins screen and notices from import to removal
body:
Parent: #10. Read it first for the goal, decisions and rules.

blocked-by: #11 (source registry, cached detection, import records and cleanup)

## Goal

From the moment another cookie plugin's data is found until the plugin **and** its leftovers are gone, the owner sees one clear next step, with a link:

| State | When | Message and links |
|---|---|---|
| `import` | Source active, its settings, scripts or pages not imported yet | {plugin} is asking your visitors now. Bring its settings across, then switch. Link: **Import from {plugin}** (Import tab, source selected) |
| `switch` | Imported; source still active | Check the import, then deactivate {plugin}: SEO Pro Cookie Consent takes over at once and visitors keep their choices. If it has a delete-data setting, turn that on first. Links: **Check the import**, **Deactivate** |
| `remove` | Source inactive or deleted; leftovers remain | {plugin} left data on the site. Links: **Delete {plugin}** (when installed), **Remove leftover data** |
| none | Plugin and data gone | Nothing |

A source that is inactive with nothing imported shows `import` with a note that pages using its documents may already be blank.

## Design

- Our consent feature waits while any source in `REPLACES` is active (decision in #10). The core `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php` already suggests deactivating replaced plugins; this child replaces that suggestion for sources that have an adapter (use the `seoprocookieconsent_replaced_plugin_extras` filter or a small hook there, without editing the core file's behaviour for other plugins), so the owner is never told to deactivate before importing.
- New class `includes/admin/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-notices.php`, reading only the cached detection and import records from #11.
  - Plugins screen (for `activate_plugins`): a note under each installed source's row (core update-note markup, as `row_note()` does) and a top notice listing every source not in the none state, including deleted plugins whose data remains.
  - The plugin's own settings screen: the same top notice. Not on other admin screens.
  - Hide per person, per `slug:state` (user meta, nonce'd `admin-post`), like `SEOProCookieConsent_Replaced_Plugins::hide()`; shows again when the state changes.
- Plain, short copy. Check `context/keywords.md` if present for the words people search ("switch from", "migrate", "import").

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/admin/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-notices.php`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-setup.php`
- EDIT: `uninstall.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`
- EDIT: `docs/architecture.md`

## Reference pattern

`admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php`: `row_note()`, `row_note_style()`, `notice()`, `hide()`, `deactivate_url()`. Reuse the patterns, not the class. Same states design: wpallstars/seoprostats#110.

## Acceptance

- Complianz active with settings: `import`; after import: `switch` with Deactivate; after deactivation: `remove`; after cleanup: nothing.
- Complianz deleted with data left: the top notice shows `remove` though there is no row.
- Hide hides only the current state. Nothing for people without `activate_plugins`. No source table or post content is queried on page load.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
- Test site with Complianz: screenshots of the Plugins screen and the settings screen in each state (never full-page).

body:
Parent: #10. Read it first for the goal, decisions and rules every adapter follows.

blocked-by: #11 (adapter base, registry, Import tab, carry-over and cleanup)

## Goal

Adapters for banners whose setup lives on the provider's servers, with a small WordPress plugin that loads their script:

- **Cookiebot by Usercentrics** (`cookiebot`, 100k+ installs).
- **iubenda** (`iubenda-cookie-law-solution`, 200k+).
- **Termly** (`uk-cookie-consent`, 80k+).

There is little to import: most settings are in the provider's dashboard, which we do not contact. The value is a clean switch: keep visitors' choices, take over blocking, replace their policy embeds, and remove what the plugin left.

## Design

- `settings()`: only what the plugin stores locally (for example blocking mode, region or Consent Mode switches); everything else is shown in the dry run as "set in {provider}'s dashboard: check these in ours" with our matching settings named.
- `scripts()`: their auto-blocking needs no list; the services our blocker finds on the site already cover the common cases. Show the services found (from the seen list) so the owner can compare with the provider's scan.
- `pages()`: their cookie declaration and policy embeds (script tags or shortcodes on pages) are replaced with our Cookie policy block; their hosted privacy policy pages stay theirs and are listed as "needs a policy of your own".
- `consent_cookie()`: read their consent cookie locally, no request. Expected and to confirm on a real install: Cookiebot `CookieConsent` (per-category flags), iubenda `_iub_cs-*` (purposes by number), Termly (cookie or local storage; carry over only if it is a cookie with explicit categories).
- No account or API key is ever asked for or stored.
- External services: none are contacted by these adapters; say so in `readme.txt` if it mentions them.

title: Banner above floating language switchers, theme-proof close button hover, optional floating Cookie settings button
body:
## What

Three front-end fixes from reviewing the merged consent engine (#3) on a Kadence site with TranslatePress:

1. **Banner hidden behind the floating language switcher.** TranslatePress's floater uses `z-index: 9999999`; the banner used `99999`, so the "English" switcher covered the bottom bar.
2. **Close (×) button turns white on hover.** Kadence styles every `button:hover, button:focus, button:active` with the theme button colours and a shadow. `.spcc-dialog__close:hover` only set a background, so the × took the theme's white text. Focus and active states of the quiet Settings button, the floating button and the embed "Cookie settings" link had the same gap.
3. **Floating Cookie settings button should be optional and off by default.** The footer-menu link is the preferred way back to Cookie settings.

## How

- `assets/css/spcc.css`: banner `z-index: var(--spcc-z, 2147483000)`; non-modal dialog fallback +1, floating button −1. Sites can override `--spcc-z` on `:root`. Hover, focus and active states set explicitly on `.spcc-btn`, `.spcc-btn--quiet`, `.spcc-embed__load`, `.spcc-dialog__close`, `.spcc-embed__settings` and `.spcc-reopen`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`: new `consent_floating_button` bool setting (default false); `footer()` prints `.spcc-reopen` only when it is on and no menu link or button was printed. `assets/js/spcc.js` already guards a missing `.spcc-reopen`.
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

No migration: nothing has been released yet.

## Verify

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`
- Preview (`scripts/preview-site.sh`), on a Kadence site with TranslatePress's floating switcher: in a Europe time zone, the banner covers the switcher; hovering and focusing the dialog's × keeps it visible in light and dark palettes; after choosing, no floating button shows until **Floating Cookie settings button** is switched on and there is no footer-menu link.

title: Settings banner preview, Cookie policy page picker, and block settings for Cookie policy and Cookie settings blocks
body:
## What

Owner requests from reviewing the merged consent engine (#3):

1. **Banner preview on the settings page**: see the banner as visitors do without leaving the Consent card.
2. **Cookie policy page as an autocomplete**: pick a page by title instead of typing its address.
3. **Gutenberg block settings where appropriate**: the Cookie policy block, and the Cookie settings block.

## How

Starter core files (`scripts/core-files.txt`: `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`, `admin/js/*`) are not changed. Everything uses plugin-owned hooks:

- **Preview:** `SEOProCookieConsent_Consent::panel()` adds a closed-by-default **Preview the banner** section. It frames the home page with `?spcc_preview=opt-in|opt-out`. For `manage_options` users only, `config()` sets the model, `preview` and sample service names. `assets/js/spcc-head.js` ignores the stored choice, and `assets/js/spcc.js` shows the banner without releasing, saving or signalling, and stops links navigating. The toolbar is hidden. `assets/js/consent-admin.js` sizes the frame for desktop or phone and reloads it after `seoprocookieconsent:setting-saved` for `consent*` keys.
- **Page picker:** `assets/js/consent-admin.js` adds jQuery UI autocomplete (core `jquery-ui-autocomplete`) to `#spcc-consent_policy_url`, over `/wp/v2/search?type=post&subtype=page`. It saves a home-relative path (already supported by `policy_url()`), and other addresses still work.
- **Blocks:** `SEOProCookieConsent_Setup::register_block()` takes `attributes` (type, default, label, options or placeholder). `assets/js/blocks.js` renders them as `InspectorControls` and passes them to `ServerSideRender`.
  - Cookie policy: introduction, Cookie settings button and last-updated date (on/off), and heading level (h2/h3/h4).
  - Cookie settings: text, and button or link.
  - The shortcodes take the same options.
- Docs: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `docs/architecture.md`.

## Verify

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`
- Preview site: Settings → SEO Pro Cookie Consent → Consent → Preview the banner. Check both visitor types and both screens, that it reloads after changing Banner position, and that choices in the frame don't set `spcc_consent`.
- Cookie policy page: type part of a page title, pick it; the field saves a path such as `/privacy-policy/`.
- Editor: the Cookie policy block sidebar toggles change the server-rendered preview; the Cookie settings block's Link style renders `<a href="#cookie-settings">`.
